narrative.title: Rewinding the Dispatch Log
narrative.scenario: A transit control console records incident reports as free-form text lines, and operators reviewing the day want the newest framing first — the log reader reverses the order of the words in each line. The raw lines are messy: extra gaps between entries, padding at either end. The rewound line must be tidy, with exactly one space between words and no padding.
narrative.inputFormat: A string s of words separated by one or more spaces, possibly with leading or trailing spaces.
narrative.outputFormat: A string with the words of s in reverse order, joined by a single space, with no leading or trailing spaces.
constraints: s contains English letters, digits, and spaces
s contains at least one word

testCases.explanation: Four cleanly separated words come back in the opposite order.
Padding at both ends is discarded, and only one space separates the reversed words.

hintLevels: Level 1: The output words are exactly the input words, only their order flips; every extra space vanishes.
Level 2: Scan the string, carve out each maximal run of visible characters, and collect the runs from right to left (or collect them all and reverse).
Level 3: Watch the edges — skip runs of spaces before and after words, and make sure consecutive words in the output are joined by exactly one space.
